conventions.view: `access` is not a §10 reduction — it is the read-side partition of §9.3, checked here as what a conforming board serves and what it reports having withheld, before any §10 reduction runs.
conventions.args: `requester` is the identity asking; `ns` selects the slice, meaning envelopes whose own namespace is `ns` or beneath it.
conventions.expect: `visible` is what the board serves. `sealed_excluded` and `participation_excluded` are the counts it MUST report for that same slice. Absent counters fail: §9.3 requires the field, and a board that omits it is indistinguishable from one claiming zero.
conventions.counted: Exactly two exclusions are counted. The seam (§8.7.5) and participation (§9.3). A no-grant denial and a blind-round denial are withheld and MUST NOT appear in any counter — a board that reports them has satisfied the arithmetic by breaking §8.3.
conventions.search_R34: `search` is the §11.3 read surface, checked here because it is the first surface with a CONTENT filter and therefore the first that could turn an exclusion count into an oracle. `args.q` is the query. The load-bearing property is that the counts DO NOT VARY with q: a conforming board evaluates the query only against envelopes the requester may read. A board that counts q-matched withheld envelopes passes every positive row here and still lets a stranger read a mailbox one character at a time.

checks.why: THE case (#199). carol holds a grant at /dm and is not a participant in bob's mailbox, so all three messages are withheld by participation. A board reporting 0 here serves a page that positively claims completeness while withholding everything in the slice — which is the defect R28 exists to remove, and it is the ordinary healthy state of every non-human band.

the operator is refused identically and counted under the seam instead, because the human branch is reached before the participation branch and the two are mutually exclusive by construction. Identical exclusion, identical total, different mechanism — the asymmetry #199 measured was that this row reported correctly and the row above did not.
the mailbox owner participates, so there is no hole in the page and nothing to count. A board reporting a non-zero count to a participant is counting the room rather than the exclusion.
each message's own author participates too, though the mailbox is not hers. Participation is per envelope, not per nest.

carol holds no grant at /vault, so the nest was never in her slice. Both the POLICY and the NOTE are withheld and NEITHER is counted. A board reporting 2 here has turned a board-wide read into a map of how much exists where the reader has no grant — the fixture has no `band:*` floor precisely so this row cannot be satisfied by accident.

the load-bearing row. bob holds a claim on /round and has not answered the round, so alice's PROPOSAL is blinded — withheld, and UNCOUNTED. The count of what a blind round withholds from a peer is the number of peers who have already answered; a board reporting 1 here tells bob he is not first, at the moment of generation, which is the herding signal §8.3 exists to suppress. The mechanism would be cancelled by its own honesty counter.
the author of a PROPOSAL is never blinded from it, so alice sees the whole round. Paired with the row above so that row cannot pass because the envelope was missing rather than withheld.

the honest zero. carol reads an ordinary nest in full, and all counters are zero — which is what makes a zero meaningful anywhere else on this fixture. A board hard-coding a non-zero participation count fails here.

search_checks.why: carol is a non-participant: all three messages are withheld, and the count is the same 3 the /read partition reports for this slice. The query matching their payloads changes nothing — it was never run against them.

THE conformance case for the oracle. Same slice, same requester, a query that cannot match anything — and the identical count. A board whose number differs between this row and the one above is answering questions about content its own ACL forbids, and each difference is one bit of a decoder.
the ordinary case: a readable envelope matches and is served, and a slice with nothing withheld reports zero rather than the board's total.

bob has not answered the open round, so alice's PROPOSAL (10) is blinded from him: neither served NOR counted, because a blinded envelope resolves to `denied` and denied envelopes are never returned for counting. The nest's own POLICY (2) DOES match and is served — its `_note` contains the word, and POLICY is seam-exempt (§8.7.4, the levers stay in the light). That contrast is the case: a readable envelope matching on content while a blinded one in the same slice leaves no trace in the results or the counters.

must_not.assert: no exclusion count on a search response varies with the query
must_not.why: the invariant the two /dm/band:bob rows sample and cannot exhaust. It must hold for every requester, every slice and every string — a board satisfying it at the sampled queries and not in general is an oracle with two known-good inputs. The check a second implementation should run: fix a requester and a slice, vary q over any set of strings, assert the counts are constant.

must_not.assert: no counter reports a blind-round exclusion
must_not.why: checked as an invariant rather than a row because it must hold at every offset and for every requester, not only where a check happens to look. This is the one exclusion whose count would defeat the mechanism producing it.

must_not.assert: no counter reports an exclusion caused by a missing read grant
must_not.why: a namespace outside your ACL was never part of your slice; counting it maps what you may not reach.

must_not.assert: a withheld envelope is never named — no page carries the id, offset or namespace of anything it excluded, in any field
must_not.why: aggregate only, ids never. The counter discloses that private traffic exists, which /dm announces by existing; it must never let a reader enumerate which offsets are private.

must_not.assert: sealed_excluded and participation_excluded are disjoint — no envelope is reported in both for the same requester
must_not.why: the human branch and the participation branch are mutually exclusive in the access path. Double-counting would inflate the gap and break the accounting the counters exist to make true.
